The Prompt Behind The Output

Role + Structured Output Prompting

نوع البرومبت المستخدم في بناء البريزنتيشن

01 — ROLE

Persona Assignment

The model is told who to be — an expert local travel planner — so tone, vocabulary and level of detail lock in before a single word is written.

02 — CONSTRAINTS

Explicit Boundaries

City, trip length, daily time blocks, transport method and a cost range are all fixed up front. Constraints remove hallucinated filler.

03 — FORMAT

Output Schema

Every day must return the same five fields: Morning, Afternoon, Evening, Transportation, Estimated cost — making the result directly slide-ready.

04 — ZERO-SHOT

No Examples Needed

No sample day was provided. Structure alone carried the instruction — the classic sign of a well-engineered zero-shot prompt.

Act as an expert local travel guide for Barcelona. Build a 5-day itinerary for a first-time visitor. For each day, return exactly: • Morning / Afternoon / Evening activities • Transportation method • Estimated daily cost in EUR Group each day around one theme (history, Gaudí, views, culture, coast). Tone: concise, practical, no filler.
Role Prompting Zero-Shot Structured Output Constraint-Based

Key Takeaways

Same Model, Better Prompt,
Better Output

A vague request ("plan me a trip to Barcelona") gives a generic paragraph. A role + constraints + schema prompt gives a structured, presentation-ready itinerary on the first try — no editing, no rewriting.
